source_batch.unit_label: CB Module F unit 2: role of primary dealers in the government securities market (courseware unit 18)

facts.statement: Evolution and eligibility of primary dealers (courseware): the objectives of the primary dealers (PDs) and satellite dealers system were to enhance the distribution channels and encourage voluntary holding of Government securities among a wider investor base, to make the government securities market vibrant, liquid and broad-based and to ensure the development of under-writing and market making capabilities for G-Sec; in 1995 the Reserve Bank introduced the system of Primary Dealers in the Government Securities Market; as on March 31, 2021 there were 21 PDs, of which 14 function as bank departments and 7 as standalone PDs (SPDs), the latter registered as NBFCs under Section 45 IA of the RBI Act, 1934; eligibility: an applicant will not be eligible if within the last one year it has been subject to litigation or regulatory action or investigation that the Reserve Bank considers material; an entity submits its application to the Chief General Manager, Internal Debt Management Department (IDMD), RBI, Mumbai; the Reserve Bank grants in principle approval and after an undertaking an authorisation letter is issued; the decision rests on RBI perception of market needs; PDs are not permitted to set up step-down subsidiaries; a PD is required to have a standing arrangement with the Reserve Bank on the execution of an undertaking and authorisation letter issued every three years, based on a fresh Board resolution; PDs submit an annual target for turnover to be achieved on behalf of mid-segment and retail investors, for the period July to June.
facts.locator: S05 courseware unit 18, printed pp. 446-447 (PDF pp. 463-464), sections 18.0 to 18.4

facts.statement: Role and liquidity support (courseware): PDs are expected to play an active role in the G-Sec market, both in primary and secondary segments, through obligations such as participating in primary auctions, market making in G-Secs, predominance of investment in G-Secs, achieving the minimum success ratio, and maintaining an efficient internal control system; standalone PDs are given liquidity support by the Reserve Bank against eligible G-Sec including SDLs, in addition to access to the LAF; half of the total liquidity support is divided equally among all the standalone PDs and the remaining 50 per cent is divided in the ratio of 1:1 based on market performance in the primary market and secondary market in the preceding six months; performance in the primary market is computed on the basis of bids accepted in T-Bill/CMB auctions and G-Sec auctions in the proportionate weights of 1 and 3; secondary market performance is judged on outright turnover in T-Bills/CMBs and G-Secs in the proportionate weights of 1 and 3; the PD-wise limit of liquidity support is revised every half-year (April-September and October-March); the liquidity support is made available at the Repo Rate announced by the Reserve Bank; it is repayable within 90 days; if it is repaid after 90 days the penal rate of interest payable by PDs is Bank rate plus 5 percentage points for the period beyond 90 days.
facts.locator: S05 courseware unit 18, printed pp. 447 (PDF p. 464), sections 18.4 and 18.5

facts.statement: Operations and performance measures (courseware): PDs are financial intermediaries mandated to take part in the development of the primary and secondary government securities market, underwrite issuances of government dated securities and participate in primary auctions; they are also mandated to achieve a minimum success ratio (bids accepted as a proportion to bidding commitment) of 40 per cent in primary auctions of T-bills and Cash Management Bills (CMBs), assessed on a half-yearly basis; the success ratio of 62.5 per cent was reported for the first half of 2021-22 in T-Bills and CMBs; all PDs individually achieved the required minimum annual total turnover ratio (both in outright and repo transactions) for Government dated securities of 5 times the average month-end stock of securities; the minimum ratio for outright transactions exclusively is 3 times; for T-Bills the corresponding minimum targets are 10 times and 6 times, respectively; the turnover ratio is the ratio of total purchase and sales during the year in the respective segment to the average month-end stocks; SPDs mobilised funds mainly by borrowings; the combined CRAR for all SPDs remained comfortably above the mandated 15 per cent.
facts.locator: S05 courseware unit 18, printed pp. 447-451 (PDF pp. 464-468), sections 18.6 and 18.7

facts.statement: Operational guidelines (courseware): PDs are subject to prudential and regulatory guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank, submit prescribed periodic returns, and the Reserve Bank can inspect the books, records and accounts; PDs are expected to join the Primary Dealers Association of India and the Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association (FIMMDA); the underwriting commitment on dated securities of Central Government is divided into two parts: a Minimum Underwriting Commitment (MUC) and an Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU); the MUC of each PD is computed to ensure that at least 50 per cent of the notified amount of each issue is mandatorily underwritten equally by all the PDs, and the share under MUC will be uniform for all PDs irrespective of capital or balance sheet size; the remaining portion is underwritten through an ACU auction; a PD cannot bid for more than 30 per cent of the notified amount in the ACU auction; in case of devolvement, PDs are allowed to set off accepted bids in the auction against their shortfall in the underwriting commitment; the Reserve Bank reserves the right to accept up to 100 per cent of the notified amount through underwriting/bidding without assigning any reason; for dated securities of State Governments (SDLs) the Reserve Bank may invite PDs to collectively underwrite up to 100 per cent of the notified amount, and a PD can underwrite up to 30 per cent of the notified amount; in T-Bills/CMB auctions each PD individually commits at the beginning of the year to submit bids for a fixed percentage of the notified amount; if a PD fails to submit the minimum bid or submits a bid lower than its commitment, the RBI may take appropriate penal action; a PD should achieve a minimum success ratio of 40 per cent of bidding commitment; for primary auction settlement, successful PDs shall provide sufficient funds in their current account with the RBI on the auction settlement day before 3:00 pm, and a shortfall is treated as an instance of SGL bouncing; PDs should offer two-way prices in G-Sec through the Negotiated Dealing System-Order Matching (NDS-OM), the OTC market and recognised stock exchanges; outright secondary market transactions in Government securities are settled on T+1 basis except those with FPIs and on NDS-OM which may be settled on T+2 basis; investment policy: PDs should frame a Board approved investment policy; investment in G-Sec should be predominant, with standalone PDs maintaining at least 50 per cent of total financial investments in G-Sec; PDs should hold their investments in G-Sec in SGL with RBI or in demat accounts with the depositories (NSDL and CDSL); all other investments such as CPs, bonds and debentures and equity instruments in demat form; HTM portfolio: standalone PDs may categorise a portion of their G-Sec portfolio as HTM, with transfers permitted only once in a year as per Board policy, quantum restricted to 100 per cent of the audited NOF as at the end of March of the preceding financial year, profit on sale credited first to the P&L Account and then appropriated to the Reserve Account, and premium amortised over the remaining period to maturity; banks undertaking PD business departmentally follow the capital adequacy and risk management guidelines applicable to banks, with the PD activity included in the bank capital adequacy framework.
facts.locator: S05 courseware unit 18, printed pp. 451-456 (PDF pp. 468-473), sections 18.8 to 18.10

payload.title: Evolution and eligibility of primary dealers
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Purpose:** widen the investor base, make the G-Sec market **liquid and broad-based**, develop **underwriting and market making**.

**History:** the **PD system began in 1995**; at **31 March 2021**: **21 PDs** (**14 bank departments, 7 standalone PDs**, SPDs registered as **NBFCs under Section 45 IA**).

**Authorisation:** apply to the **CGM, IDMD, RBI Mumbai**; **in principle approval**, then an **authorisation letter**; **undertaking** renewed **every three years**; **no step-down subsidiaries**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Authorisation depends on RBI's view of market needs and a clean record over the previous year. Continuation depends on compliance with the terms of authorisation.

self_check.prompt_text: In which year did the Reserve Bank introduce primary dealers?

payload.title: Role of PDs and RBI liquidity support
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Role:** primary auctions, market making, predominant G-Sec investment, **minimum success ratio**, efficient internal control.

**Liquidity support (SPDs):** **half shared equally** among SPDs; the other **50% split 1:1** between primary and secondary performance of the last six months; **weights 1 and 3** for T-Bill/CMB and G-Sec performance; limits revised **half-yearly**; priced at the **repo rate**; repay within **90 days**, else **Bank Rate + 5 percentage points**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The scheme rewards PDs that perform in both primary and secondary markets. It is available against eligible G-Secs including SDLs and is separate from LAF access.

self_check.prompt_text: At what rate is the liquidity support to SPDs made available?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The Repo Rate announced by the Reserve Bank.

payload.title: Performance measures of PDs
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Success ratio:** bids accepted ÷ bidding commitment, minimum **40 per cent** in T-Bill and CMB auctions, assessed **half-yearly**.

**Turnover ratio:** total purchase and sales ÷ average month-end stock; minimum **5 times** (outright and repo) and **3 times** (outright only) for dated securities; **10 times** and **6 times** for T-Bills/CMBs.

**Capital:** SPD CRAR mandated at **15 per cent**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: These ratios keep PDs active in both the primary and secondary market. The courseware tables of performance values are dated and are not taught here.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the minimum annual total turnover ratio for dated securities?

payload.title: Underwriting, bidding, secondary market and investment guidelines
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Underwriting:** **MUC** (at least **50% of the notified amount**, shared equally) plus **ACU** auction (a PD cannot bid for more than **30%** of notified amount); RBI may accept up to **100%**; **devolvement** is set off against accepted ACU bids.

**SDLs:** PDs may underwrite up to **100%** collectively, **30%** per PD.

**T-Bills/CMBs:** yearly **bidding commitment**; **success ratio 40 per cent**; penal action on shortfall.

**Settlement:** funds in the current account by **3:00 pm** on the auction day; **SGL bouncing** if short; outright secondary trades **T+1** (FPIs and NDS-OM **T+2**).

**Investments:** at least **50%** of financial investments in G-Sec; G-Sec in **SGL or demat**; **HTM** up to **100% of audited NOF**, one transfer a year.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Banks running PD business departmentally apply the bank's own capital adequacy and risk framework. Auditors must certify compliance with the HTM instructions.

self_check.prompt_text: What share of the notified amount is the minimum underwriting commitment (MUC)?
self_check.expected_takeaway: At least 50 per cent, underwritten equally by all PDs.

items.title: Evolution and eligibility of primary dealers
items.core_explanation_md:
**Purpose:** widen the investor base, make the G-Sec market **liquid and broad-based**, develop **underwriting and market making**.

**History:** the **PD system began in 1995**; at **31 March 2021**: **21 PDs** (**14 bank departments, 7 standalone PDs**, SPDs registered as **NBFCs under Section 45 IA**).

**Authorisation:** apply to the **CGM, IDMD, RBI Mumbai**; **in principle approval**, then an **authorisation letter**; **undertaking** renewed **every three years**; **no step-down subsidiaries**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Authorisation depends on RBI's view of market needs and a clean record over the previous year. Continuation depends on compliance with the terms of authorisation.

items.title: Role of PDs and RBI liquidity support
items.core_explanation_md:
**Role:** primary auctions, market making, predominant G-Sec investment, **minimum success ratio**, efficient internal control.

**Liquidity support (SPDs):** **half shared equally** among SPDs; the other **50% split 1:1** between primary and secondary performance of the last six months; **weights 1 and 3** for T-Bill/CMB and G-Sec performance; limits revised **half-yearly**; priced at the **repo rate**; repay within **90 days**, else **Bank Rate + 5 percentage points**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The scheme rewards PDs that perform in both primary and secondary markets. It is available against eligible G-Secs including SDLs and is separate from LAF access.

items.title: Performance measures of PDs
items.core_explanation_md:
**Success ratio:** bids accepted ÷ bidding commitment, minimum **40 per cent** in T-Bill and CMB auctions, assessed **half-yearly**.

**Turnover ratio:** total purchase and sales ÷ average month-end stock; minimum **5 times** (outright and repo) and **3 times** (outright only) for dated securities; **10 times** and **6 times** for T-Bills/CMBs.

**Capital:** SPD CRAR mandated at **15 per cent**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: These ratios keep PDs active in both the primary and secondary market. The courseware tables of performance values are dated and are not taught here.

items.title: Underwriting, bidding, secondary market and investment guidelines
items.core_explanation_md:
**Underwriting:** **MUC** (at least **50% of the notified amount**, shared equally) plus **ACU** auction (a PD cannot bid for more than **30%** of notified amount); RBI may accept up to **100%**; **devolvement** is set off against accepted ACU bids.

**SDLs:** PDs may underwrite up to **100%** collectively, **30%** per PD.

**T-Bills/CMBs:** yearly **bidding commitment**; **success ratio 40 per cent**; penal action on shortfall.

**Settlement:** funds in the current account by **3:00 pm** on the auction day; **SGL bouncing** if short; outright secondary trades **T+1** (FPIs and NDS-OM **T+2**).

**Investments:** at least **50%** of financial investments in G-Sec; G-Sec in **SGL or demat**; **HTM** up to **100% of audited NOF**, one transfer a year.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Banks running PD business departmentally apply the bank's own capital adequacy and risk framework. Auditors must certify compliance with the HTM instructions.
